kernels.l1: In a tidy machine, nobody has to share a cubby.
kernels.l2: A machine that never sends two things to the same place is a no-sharing machine. Every arrowhead has at most one arrow landing on it.
kernels.l3: A function is one-to-one when different inputs always give different answers. The useful way to check it is backwards: if two inputs give the same answer, they must have been the same input.
kernels.l4: f is injective when s₁ ≠ s₂ ⇒ f(s₁) ≠ f(s₂), equivalently f(s₁) = f(s₂) ⇒ s₁ = s₂. The contrapositive form is the one used in proofs. Each t ∈ T has at most one pre-image.
kernels.l5: Injectivity says the pre-image of every singleton has at most one element; the contrapositive form is what proofs actually use.
kernels.l6: An injection is left-cancellable: f(s₁) = f(s₂) forces s₁ = s₂, so f has a left inverse on its image.
kernels.l7: f is injective when equal outputs force equal inputs; the contrapositive form is the working definition, and it says every fibre f⁻¹({t}) has at most one point.
kernels.l8: Injections are the monomorphisms of Set; injectivity is equivalent to left-cancellability and, for nonempty domains, to the existence of a left inverse.
